findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A documentation-only change merges a newer default-branch commit that changed code, and its check receives the older event base.
Close records a light review against the merged default, but this call passes the older event base to `blocking_level` as well as to the fingerprint. `src/forge/review.py:172` and `src/forge/docskip.py:113` consequently include the unrelated default-branch code in the docs-only classification. The check treats the light review as no longer allowed and rejects it as out of date. Full reviews can also be rejected: `src/forge/review.py:163` reads the functional-check paragraph from the older base, so a newer default-branch commit can replace the worker's paragraph in the fingerprint.
The unmet Done-when line is: tests/test_aha_review.py passes on the default branch, and a clean review still passes forge-pr-check when the event's base is older than the default branch the change merged.

The named older-base proof changes `app.py` at `tests/test_pr_check_base_older_than_merged_default.py:9-12`, so it exercises a full review and can pass while the light-review case is rejected. The light-review test at `tests/test_docs_and_assets_get_light_checks.py:103-117` checks against the current base instead. The command-level proof needs to cover their interaction.
